newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's Petrom RA to administer oil blocks.
newsitem.headline: Romania's Petrom RA to administer oil blocks.

text.p: In a move to restructure the oil sector, Romania's Petrom RA oil authority has signed an accord with the National Agency for Mineral Resources to administer the oil blocks it operates, a company official said.
"This is an attempt to bring the oil sector closer to market economy realities," Petrom vice president Marius Velescu said after the signing ceremony on Tuesday.

Under the accord, Petrom would take in its administration the 19 oil blocks it operates and the company would be placed on an equal footing with the foreign oil firms operating in Romania, Velescu said.

The move is part of a programme aimed at restructuring Petrom -- now a government-controlled regie autonome -- and turn it into a commercial company, with hopes to maintain crude oil output at present levels.
Petrom is responsible for exploration and production of crude oil and associated natural gas. Its oil and gas output covers some 30 percent of Romania's energy resources.

The 19 blocks also include prospective oil areas on which Petrom would perform exploratory drillings in order to identify oil deposits, Velescu said, adding that Petrom was "open" to co-operation with foreign companies in the sector.
The Agency for Mineral Resources is a regulatory and licensing authority in charge of mineral rights administration.
Under the accord, Petrom would carry out "exploration works whose volume should not be lower than those performed out by foreign oil companies operating in Romania."
Last year, Petrom spent $265 million in exploration projects and invested $50 million in research, data show.
Velescu said Petrom's immediate plans included a split of the activities within the company, in order to make it more efficient and create competition in the sector.
"We will separate the exploration and extraction sectors from the repairs, maintenance and other auxiliary services which now employ 50 percent of Petrom's 62,000 staff," he said.

Romania, a mature oil and gas producing region which began commercial production of oil in the 1860s, has seen a constant decline in its output over the past years, mainly due to frenzied exploitation of oil and gas reserves and use of poor equipment under the former communist regime, ousted in 1989.
The country recently issued legislation to protect foreign investment, a new petroleum law putting local and foreign firms on equal footing and a bill allowing foreigners to buy land.
Romania's crude production was some 6.7 million tonnes last year, compared to a peak output of 14.7 million in 1986.
"Our hope is to maintain output over the next decade at a level close to last year's production," a Petrom official said.
